messages:
Maya (Support): Customer reported assistant call failing when it streams tool arguments — final JSON object gets cut mid-field and we return a schema validation error. customer cid=cid-98765, sample logs attached below. They see it on production intermittently, ~1 in 500 requests.

Priya (Support Eng): Do we know if they're using websocket or HTTP streaming? Any proxy in front of our ingest?

Maya (Support): They're using HTTP/1.1 chunked transfer behind a third-party L7 proxy. Proxy config says keepalives enabled. They pasted our raw log capture: 
```
2026-03-17T10:02:12.941Z INFO ingest id=cid-98765 recv_chunk=4096 last=false
payload={"tool":"charge","args":{"order_id":12345,"amount":1999,"currency":"USD","card":\{"last4":"4242","exp":"12/26"}...
```
The JSON ends with ellipsis when the request stream closes. Our server replies with `400 schema_validation_error` and stack: `EOF while parsing object`

Jared (Runtime Eng): That looks like a mid-chunk boundary where the client/proxy closes the TCP frame before the final bytes reach our reassembly buffer. I pulled the ingestion traces — see this snippet from staging: 
```
[ingest] ts=2026-03-17T09:58:10Z id=cid-98765 frame=0 bytes=4096 more=true
[ingest] ts=2026-03-17T09:58:10Z id=cid-98765 frame=1 bytes=1024 more=false
payload tail: "\"card\":{\"last4\":\"4242\",\"exp\":\"12/26\"}\n```
We end up with an incomplete trailing fragment when the L7 does a flush mid-object.

Lina (Infra): Reproduced locally by toggling NGINX `proxy_request_buffering off;` + connection reuse. When the upstream flushes, nginx can send a chunk boundary right after a random byte. If the runtime assumes a full JSON per-chunk, it will try to parse too early. I can repro with a small script that streams partial JSON frames.

Priya (Support Eng): Can you paste the repro script? Customer wants a mitigation now — recommended temporary workaround?

Jared (Runtime Eng): Repro script: 
```bash
python -c "import sys,socket,time; s=socket.create_connection(('ingest.prod',443)); s.send(b'POST /v1/stream HTTP/1.1\r\nHost: ingest.prod\r\nTransfer-Encoding: chunked\r\n\r\n4\r\n{\"t\":\"\"\r\n6\r\nool\":\r\n8\r\n{\"a\":1\r\n0\r\n\r\n')\n# simulates chunk split in the middle of an object\n"
```
Temporary mitigation: ask customer to disable request streaming (send full payload in one request) or enable a small client-side buffer so we don't get mid-object flushes. On our side, I'll add a short reassembly buffer that delays parsing until either the chunked stream ends or we see a JSON-complete parse.

Maya (Support): Customer prefers server-side fix. Any ETA? They report this is hitting payments flow and is urgent.

Jared (Runtime Eng): I'll do a quick patch in runtime to buffer up to 16KB and attempt streaming-aware parse; if incomplete, wait up to 2s for remainder before failing. I can have a mitigation rollout to staging in ~3 hrs, production after testing in ~8 hrs.

Lina (Infra): Also going to file a policy note for proxy partners: avoid mid-object flushes for JSON bodies or set `proxy_request_buffering on` for endpoints that expect JSON in chunked streams.

ingest-bot: created ticket RH-1234 (runtime/ingest) for "half-frame JSON arg truncation on chunked streams" and linked to customer cid-98765.

Priya (Support Eng): Marking customer P1 for now, will reply with the workaround and ETA. Will attach repro steps and the ingest-bot ticket.

Maya (Support): Thanks — I'll update the customer and ask them to try the non-streaming fallback in the meantime. Please ping here when staging patch is up so I can validate. :pray:
